description: baseline

Build a CUTE DSL blocked QR implementation for large n=1024-4096 with panel factorization plus trailing update tiles, prioritizing fewer torch/LAPACK launches and coalesced shared-memory staging while returning exact geqrf-style compact Householder factors.
Added guarded CUTE DSL large-QR scaffold with safe torch.geqrf fallback; validates and benchmarks marginally faster/noise-equivalent while CUTE is unavailable locally.

Added large upper-triangular identity-Householder fast path after CUTE guard; correct, but full benchmark regressed because detection overhead hits all large dense shapes and benchmark has no upper case.
Removed the measured-regressing upper-triangular detection path, restoring the guarded CUTE scaffold plus torch.geqrf fallback as the best correct branch state.

Best score reached was 114988.669 us at commit 47e2e025 with a guarded CUTE DSL large-QR scaffold and torch.geqrf fallback; final branch HEAD 9d0acb32 keeps that same code after reverting a measured-regressing upper-triangular detection experiment. CUTE/CUTLASS Python DSL is not installed in this host environment, so the custom CUTE path cannot actually compile or run here; all correct measured performance is fallback torch.geqrf/noise. The large upper-triangular fast path validated but regressed the active benchmark to 115826.352 us because detection overhead penalized all large dense benchmark shapes and the benchmark active set has no upper-triangular case. Next useful brief should either install/vendor CUTE or switch to an available kernel language/library path; without CUTE available, further CUTE DSL work is limited to guarded scaffolding rather than executable optimization.

Combine 49decc and 11c593: integrate the n=32 custom Householder QR fast path with the n=512/1024 rank-deficient short-factor/padded compact-output path, resolving dispatch/output-shape conflicts and preserving full validation; only clean up guarded CUDA/CUTLASS/CUTE scaffolding when it is executable in this environment, with no unavailable DSL-only code.

Integrated the n=32 custom Householder CUDA fast path from 49decc with the n=512/1024 rank-deficient short-factor padded-output path from 11c593; full validation passed and benchmark improved to 108248.964 us.

Removed the inherited n=4096 upper-triangular detector/CUTLASS-CUTE availability probe since it was executable CUDA but regressed dense 4096 and was not useful for the active benchmark; cleaned combo improved to 106833.609 us.
Tried a two-stage rank-deficient detector to avoid scanning full tails on dense n=512/1024, but benchmark was noise/slightly worse at 106871.829 us versus the simpler cleaned combo.

Reverted the staged detector and restored the simpler full-tail rankdef check; full validation passed and best measured score improved to 106234.553 us, with gains from qr32 plus rankdef and no n=4096 probe overhead.

Best score reached was 106234.553 us at final commit eaf3c7c1. The successful combine integrates 49decc's executable n=32 inline-CUDA Householder kernel with 11c593's n=512/1024 rank-deficient short-factor padded compact-output path, then removes the inherited n=4096 upper-triangular probe and unavailable CUTLASS/CUTE import scaffolding. The upper probe was executable but harmful on the active dense 4096 benchmark, and a staged rankdef detector also failed to improve; final state keeps only executable useful custom CUDA plus torch.geqrf fallback. Suggested next brief: pursue a real executable larger-n custom kernel path (CUTE only if installed/vendorized) or specialize rankdef detection/factorization further without host synchronizations.

Combine 2c0f05's n=176 custom CUDA QR path with eaf3c7's cleaned n=32 and n=512/1024 rank-deficient short-factor paths, preserving shape-only dispatch and excluding upper/CUTE probes. First validate and benchmark all stacked executable paths for regressions; only then profile n=352 as the next medium-size target.
Stacked 2c0f05 n=176 global-memory CUDA QR with eaf3c7 cleaned n=32 and n=512/1024 rankdef paths, removed upper/CUTE probes, full validation passed, benchmark 103831.705 us.

Tried a direct n=352 global-memory Householder CUDA kernel modeled on qr176; validation passed but benchmark regressed badly to 110448.437 us because n=352 shape slowed to ~79.9 ms versus torch.geqrf ~38 ms.
Reverted the regressing QR352 experiment, restoring the stacked executable qr32+qr176+rankdef paths; full validation passed and final benchmark measured 103867.457 us.

Best score reached in this brief was 103831.705 us at 711c1636 when stacking executable n=32, n=176, and n=512/1024 rankdef paths; final HEAD bab5f98a keeps the same effective implementation after reverting the failed n=352 experiment, with final remeasure 103867.457 us. The required n=352 profile was captured; a direct global-memory QR352 kernel validated but was much slower, increasing n=352 to ~79.9 ms and geomean to 110448.437 us, so it was reverted. No CUTE DSL code was kept because the DSL remains unavailable; next useful direction is a different medium-size algorithm for n=352 (blocked/tiled, library-backed, or CUTE only if executable) rather than scaling the one-CTA QR176 design.

From global-best 7d34d85, pursue a fresh n=352 macro path unlike the failed one-CTA global-memory Householder: implement a blocked panel QR with tiled trailing-update kernels/shared-memory panels, preserving existing n=32/n=176/rankdef/mixed dispatch; profile the minimal executable path and abandon if n352 remains slower than torch.geqrf.

Implemented a minimal blocked n=352 panel path using 88-column geqrf panels and ormqr trailing updates; validation passed but n352 slowed to ~118.9 ms and geomean regressed to 107252.100 us, so the path is not viable.
Reverted the blocked n=352 panel path after it proved slower than torch.geqrf; restored global-best dispatch and remeasured final head at 97437.788 us.

Brief exhausted. Tried a fresh blocked n=352 macro path from global-best 7d34d85 using 88-column geqrf panels and ormqr trailing updates; it validated but n352 slowed to ~118.9 ms and geomean regressed to 107252.100 us, so it was abandoned/reverted. Final HEAD adbc4f06 restores the global-best implementation and remeasured at 97437.788 us; final n352 profile is saved. CUTE DSL is still unavailable in this environment, so no CUTE-only code was kept. Next n352 work should avoid multi-launch panelization and either use an executable fused/tiled custom kernel with fewer global-memory passes or leave torch.geqrf as the fallback.

On parent 6733ae57, specialize only the n1024 near-rank case: add a conservative cheap CUDA-side detector for trailing-column dependence, factor a safe leading subspace with contract-preserving padded output, and fall back unchanged for dense n1024 and all existing n32/n176/rankdef/clustered/mixed paths; reject any detector overhead that hurts dense n1024.

Added CUDA-side n1024 near-rank detector comparing trailing columns to leading columns and reduced QR/padded output, but validation failed on n1024 nearrank because padded leading-subspace QR does not preserve the full compact factorization residual.
Reverted invalid n1024 nearrank detector, restoring parent behavior; validation passed and benchmark measured 94856.031 us, consistent with parent run noise.

Brief exhausted. A CUDA-side n1024 near-rank detector correctly identified the case but the reduced leading-subspace padded-output shortcut was invalid: validation failed on n1024 nearrank with a large R - Q.T@A residual, so it was logged as validation_error and reverted. Final HEAD e400188c restores parent behavior, validates, benchmarks at 94856.031 us, and has a final n1024-nearrank profile saved. The near-rank structure cannot be handled by simply factoring the first 3n/4 columns and padding; next work would need a mathematically valid low-rank/column-dependence compact factor reconstruction or should leave torch.geqrf for nearrank.

Explore a separate large-square dense QR fallback for n2048/n4096 using torch/cusolver workspace and output handling more directly than the current geqrf wrapper: profile allocation, copy, and factorization boundaries, then restructure only the large dense dispatch to avoid redundant materialization and postprocessing; preserve all existing small, n176, rank-deficient, mixed, and classifier-sensitive paths.
Specialized n2048/n4096 dense fallback to preallocate geqrf out buffers (h,tau), avoiding PyTorch allocating outputs internally; validation passed and full benchmark measured 93594.454 us.

Reverted the n2048/n4096 geqrf out-buffer specialization after focused wrapped timing showed out= slightly slower than default torch.geqrf; validation passed and full benchmark improved to 93192.131 us.

Specialized n2048/n4096 to call torch.ops.aten.geqrf.default directly after focused probes showed parity/slight wins, but full validation+benchmark regressed to 93477.267 us, with n4096 slower than default torch.geqrf.
Restored default torch.geqrf for n2048/n4096 after ATen direct dispatch regressed; validation passed and full benchmark remeasured at 93192.276 us, matching the best large-dense fallback result.

Brief exhausted. Explored large dense n2048/n4096 QR dispatch/output handling from parent f9411990: preallocated torch.geqrf out buffers validated but regressed to 93594.454 us and focused wrapped probes showed out= was slightly slower; direct torch.ops.aten.geqrf.default validated but full benchmark regressed to 93477.267 us, especially n4096. Final HEAD b841f448 restores the default torch.geqrf large fallback, validates, benchmarks at 93192.276 us (best in this brief, matching the revert run at 93192.131 us), and has final n2048 NCU profile saved at autocuda/profiles/2026-06-24-03-03-06-qrv2_kernel_languages_96364acw1/worker-1-brief-5-final-b841f44891e52442fc1009ce36e82647a93bd659-n2048.ncu-txt. CUTE/CUTLASS DSL remains unavailable here, so no DSL-only code was kept; next large-dense work likely needs lower-level cuSOLVER binding or a different structural case, not PyTorch geqrf wrapper variants.

Combine 91d345's n176 16-column tiled trailing-update win with fb0081's rankdef-first structural classifier bandwidth win: use 91d345 as base, transplant only fb0081's rankdef-first precedence/short-circuit classifier changes, preserve n32, mixed-split, dense fallback, and n176 tiled behavior, then validate and benchmark the pure stack before any further edits.

Combined 91d345 n176 16-column tiled trailing updates with fb0081 rankdef-first structural classifier short-circuit only; validation passed and full benchmark measured 93172.362 us, a small improvement over either parent/noise band.

Completed the exact fb0081 rankdef-first classifier transplant on top of 91d345 by adding the per-thread clustered scan early-exit guard; validation passed and full benchmark improved to 92511.772 us.

Brief exhausted. Combined 91d345's n176 16-column tiled trailing-update implementation with fb0081's rankdef-first structural classifier. The initial transplant validated and benchmarked at 93172.362 us; adding the exact fb0081 per-thread clustered scan early-exit guard preserved correctness and improved the full benchmark to 92511.772 us. Final HEAD b35a9d71 validates, benchmarks best in this brief, preserves n32/mixed/dense/n176 behavior, and has final n512-rankdef NCU profile at autocuda/profiles/2026-06-24-03-03-06-qrv2_kernel_languages_96364acw1/worker-1-brief-6-final-b35a9d713f1a92a53ccb17d9af71623294181e9f-n512-rankdef.ncu-txt. CUTE/CUTLASS DSL remains unavailable, so no DSL-only code was used.

From 87d8, prototype an executable load_inline CUDA reduced-QR path only for all-eligible n512 rankdef batches: specialize to the detected leading width used by the existing reduced torch.geqrf path, preserve compact geqrf output padding/layout plus n176/n32/classifier/mixed/dense fallbacks, benchmark against reduced torch.geqrf, and abandon before n1024/mixed if n512 rankdef is not faster.

Prototyped a load_inline CUDA Householder path for all-rankdef n512 using rank=384 padded compact output, but differential guards failed on n512 rankdef cases with large R-Q.T@A residuals, so the prototype is invalid and must be fixed or abandoned before benchmarking.

Added synchronization after each 16-column update in the CUDA n512 rankdef QR prototype, but differential guards still failed on rankdef matrices with large R-Q.T@A residuals; the custom all-eligible n512 path remains invalid.

Abandoned the invalid custom CUDA n512 rankdef QR prototype and restored the parent reduced torch.geqrf rankdef path; validation passed and benchmark measured 91356.847 us, so no custom n512 rankdef path is kept.

Brief exhausted. From 87d8, I prototyped an executable load_inline CUDA Householder QR for all-eligible n512 rankdef batches using rank=384 padded compact output, but validation guards failed with large R-Q.T@A residuals. A synchronization fix after each 16-column trailing update still failed the same rankdef differential cases, so the custom path was abandoned before any n1024/mixed expansion. Final HEAD 045362ef restores the parent reduced torch.geqrf rankdef path, validates, benchmarks at 91356.847 us, and has final n512-rankdef profile at autocuda/profiles/2026-06-24-03-03-06-qrv2_kernel_languages_96364acw1/worker-1-brief-7-final-045362ef0251ba32c4d49b036ac31fc20f71a731-n512-rankdef.ncu-txt. CUTE/CUTLASS DSL is still unavailable; next work should avoid scaling this one-CTA Householder design to n512 without a stronger numerical/correctness strategy.

Micro-tune only the existing executable n32 CUDA QR fast path on 87d8d1f: profile the current single-block Householder kernel and reduce launch/body overhead with warp-only reductions, fewer barriers, fixed-32 loop unrolling, and safe tau/output store trimming; do not alter routing, classifier, n176, mixed, dense, or n512 paths; keep only if validation passes and both n32 bucket and full geomean improve.

Replaced qr32 shared-memory reductions with warp shuffle reductions to reduce barriers, but validation failed on n32 with a large R-Q.T@A residual, so the warp-only change is incorrect and must be fixed or reverted.
